sentences.text:
The present petition is filed with a prayer to grant statutory interest under Section 80 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 (in short as 'the Act' 2013') on the compensation amount awarded under the Award dated 28.06.2016 in Land Acquisition Case No. 312 of 2013 as also on the amended Award dated 02.05.2019.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/13998/2024 ORDER DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined 2.
We may note that the petitioners have not raised any dispute with regard to non-inclusion of statutory interest in the award which was passed on 28.06.2016.
Even this issue was not raised at the time when claim for multiplier of Factor 2 was raised and amended Award was passed on 02.05.2019.

After a period of 8 years from the date of the original award and almost 6 years from the date of the amended award, for the first time, the instant petition has been filed on the premise that in identical matter, by judgement and order dated 02.07.2024, this Court has directed the respondents to pay the statutory interest as prescribed under Section 80 of the Act' 2013.

3. There is complete silence in the writ petition about the interest amount, if any, paid to the petitioners under the award in question which states that in case the possession of the land in question had been taken by the acquiring body, interest was required to be paid.

4. We, therefore, do not accept the oral arguments made by the learned counsel for the petitioner at the Bar without any supporting statement in the writ petition that no amount of interest has been paid to the petitioners.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/13998/2024 ORDER DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined 5.
It is admitted that the circular of the State Government provided for payment of interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of dispossession of the date of making payment.
6. No grievance, however, had been raised by the petitioners for a sufficient long time, i.e. for 8 years.
For this reason, we are of the considered opinion that the petitioners have acquiesced with the compensation determined under the award dated 28.06.2016.

The dead claim sought to be revived on the basis of the order dated 02.07.2024 would cause burden on the State exchequer, inasmuch as, any additional amount towards interest under Section 80 of the Act' 2013 has to be paid out of the public money.
Once acquiesced with the determination made under the award dated 28.06.2016, the petitioners cannot be permitted to revive a dead claim on the premise of similar order passed by this Court.

7. The fact that in one of the matters, the interest at the rate of 9% and 15% under Section 80 of the Act' 2013 was directed to be added in the award dated 31.03.2023 would not be a reason to pass similar order in the present case, as no plausible submission could be made by the learned advocate for the petitioners for explaining NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/13998/2024 ORDER DATED:
30/09/2024 undefined the latches on the part of the petitioners, i.e. the claim of the petitioners being dead after a period of 8 years.
